(D) is true

questions.question: When subject to a unit step input, the closed loop control system shown in the figure will have a steady state error of
questions.explanation:
Using signal flow graph,



Forward path gains
\(P_{1}=\left ( -1 \right )\times \frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{-2}{s+2}\) and
\(P_2=\frac{3}{s}\frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{6}{s(s+2)}\)
Individual loop,
\(L_1=-1 \times \frac{3}{s}\times \frac{2}{s+2}=\frac{-6}{s(s+2)}\)
Loop touches forward paths, therefore,
\(\Delta _1=1 \text{ and } \Delta _2=1\)
\(D=1-L_1 =1+\frac{6}{s(s+2)}=\frac{s(s+2)+6}{s(s+2)}\)
Using Mason's gain formula,
\(\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)}=\frac{P_1\Delta _1+P_2\Delta _2}{\Delta } =\frac{-\frac{2}{s+2}\times 1+\frac{6}{s(s+2)}\times 1}{\frac{s(s+2)+6}{s(s+2)}}\)
\(\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)}=\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6}\)
For unit step input, \(R(s)=\frac{1}{s}\)
\[\begin{aligned} Y(s)&=R(s)\cdot \left ( \frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ) \\ Error&=E(s)=R(s)-Y(s) \\&=R(s)-R(s)\left (\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ) \\ &=R(s)\left [ 1-\frac{6-2s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ]\\ E(s)&=\frac{1}{s}\left [ \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ] \end{aligned}\]
Steady state value of error, using final value theoram,
\[\begin{aligned}e_{ss}&=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}sE(s) \\ &=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}s\left [ \frac{1}{s}\cdot \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ] \\ &=\lim_{s\rightarrow 0}\left [ \frac{s^2+4s}{s^2+2s+6} \right ]=0 \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
For the matrix
\[p=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2&2 \\ 0& -2 & 1\\ 0 &0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
one of the eigen values is equal to -2. Which of the following is an eigen vector ?
questions.explanation:
Since matrix is triangular, the eigen values are the diagonal elements themselves namely \(\lambda =3, -2\) and 1.
Corresponding to eigen value \(\lambda = -2\) let us find the eigen vector
\([A-\lambda I]\hat{x}=0\)
\[\begin{bmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 & 2\\ 0 & -2-\lambda & 1\\ 0& 0 & 1-\lambda \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
Putting \(\lambda = -2\) in above equation we get,
\[\begin{bmatrix} 5 & -2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & 1\\ 0& 0 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_1\\ x_2\\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
Which gives the equations,
\[\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\\ 3x_3&=0 \;\;...(iii) \end{aligned}\]
Since equation (ii) and (iii) are same we have
\[\begin{aligned} 5x_1-2x_2+2x_3&=0 \;\;...(i)\\ x_3 &=0 \;\;...(ii)\end{aligned}\] Putting \(x_2=k\), we get

\(x =0\) or \(x=2\) are the stationary points.
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Now, } f''(x) &= e^{-x}(2-2x)+(2x-x^2)(-e^{-x})\\ &= e^{-x}(2-2x-(2x-x^2))\\ &= e^{-x}(x^2-4x+2)\\ At\;x=0& \\ f''(0)&= e^{-0}(0-0+2)=2 \end{aligned}\]

Now at \(x=2\)

\(\therefore \;\; At \;\; x=2\) we have a maxima.

The resultant air-gap flux per pole is given by
\(\phi _r=\frac{1}{4.44k_{\omega _1}N_{pn_1}}\left ( \frac{V}{f} \right )\)
\(\phi _r\propto \left ( \frac{V}{f} \right )\)

Let, \(V_0=\) Nominal voltage
\(f_0=\) Nominal frequency

\[\begin{aligned} V &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right ) V_0\\ X'_2 &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right ) X'_{20} \\ \omega _s &=\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )\omega _{20} \\ T_{max}&= \frac{3}{\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )\omega _{s_0}}\left [ \frac{0.5 \left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )^2 V_0^2}{\left ( \frac{f}{f_0} \right )X'_{20}} \right ]\\ &= \frac{3}{\omega _{s_0}}\frac{0.5V_0^2}{X'_{20}}\\ &=\text{constant, independent of f} \end{aligned}\]

questions.question: The figure shows the voltage across a power semiconductor device and the current through the device during a switching transitions. Is the transition a turn ON transition or a turn OFF transition ? What is the energy lost during the transition ?
questions.explanation:
During interval \(t_2\), voltage starts decreasing and becomes zero and current starts increasing and becomes constant (I), so transition is turn on.

During \(t_1\) interval:
Power loss \(=vi\)
\(E_1=\text{Energy loss}=\int vi\; dt=V\int i\; dt\)
V is constant during this period v=V
\(\int i\; dt\) represents area under i-t curve
\(\int i\; dt=\frac{1}{2} \times I \times t_1\)
\(E_1=V\int i\; dt=\frac{1}{2} V I t_1\;\;...(i)\)
During \(t_2\) interval:
Power loss = vi
\(E_2=\text{Energy loss}=\int vi\; dt=I\int v\; dt\)
i is constant during this period i=I
\(\int v\; dt\) represents area under v-t curve
\(\int v\; dt=\frac{1}{2} VIt_2\)
\(E_2=I\int v\; dt=\frac{1}{2} V I t_2\;\;...(ii)\)
Total energy lost during the transition
\(E=E_1+E_2\)
\(E=\frac{1}{2}VIt_1+\frac{1}{2}VIt_2\)

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question:
A state variable system
\[\dot{X}\left ( t \right )=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}X\left ( t \right )+ \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}u\left ( t \right )\],
with the initial condition \[X\left ( 0 \right )=\begin{bmatrix} -1, &3 \end{bmatrix}^{T}\] and the unit step input \(u\left ( t \right )\) has

The state transition matrix
questions.explanation:
\[\dot{x}(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &-1 \\ 0& -3 \end{bmatrix}x(t)+\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}V(t) \;\;...(i)\]
\(\dot{x}(t)=Ax(t)+Bu(t) \;\;...(ii)\)
Comparing equation (i) and (ii), we get
\[A= \text{System matrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 0 &-3 \end{bmatrix}\] and \[B=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[\begin{aligned}[sI-A]&=\begin{bmatrix} s &0 \\ 0 & s \end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix} 0 &1 \\ 0 &-3 \end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} s &-1 \\ s &s+3 \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\frac{\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &1 \\ 0 &s \end{bmatrix}}{s(s+3)-0x(-1)} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{s(s+3)}\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \\ [sI-A]^{-1}&=\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{3}\left ( \frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s+3} \right )\\ 0 &\frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \\ &\text{State transition matrix } \\ &=L^{-1}[(sI-A)^{-1}]\\ \phi (t)&=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &\frac{1}{3}(1-e^{-3t}) \\ 0& e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question:
A state variable system
\[\dot{X}\left ( t \right )=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1\\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix}X\left ( t \right )+ \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}u\left ( t \right )\],
with the initial condition \[X\left ( 0 \right )=\begin{bmatrix} -1, &3 \end{bmatrix}^{T}\] and the unit step input \(u\left ( t \right )\) has

the state transition equation
questions.explanation:
ZIR (zero Input Response) \(=\phi (t) \times X(0)\)
\[=\begin{bmatrix} 1 &\frac{}{3}(1-e^{-3t}) \\ 0& e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} -1\\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[=\begin{bmatrix} -1+1-e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} -e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}\]
ZSR (Zero State Response)
\(=L^{-1}[(sI-A)^{-1}BU(s)]\)
\[=L^{-1}\left \{ \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s} & \frac{1}{s(s+3)}\\ 0& \frac{1}{s+3} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\frac{1}{s}\right \}\]
\[=l^{-1}\begin{bmatrix} 1/s^2\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} t\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\]
\(\therefore\) State transition equation
\[\;\;\; =ZIR+ZSR=\begin{bmatrix} -e^{-3t} \\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix} t\\0 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[\;\;\;=\begin{bmatrix} t-e^{-3t}\\ 3 e^{-3t} \end{bmatrix}\]

questions.question:
A 1000 kVA , 6.6 kV, 3-phase star connected cylindrical pole synchronous generator has a synchronous reactance of 20\(\Omega\). Neglect the armature resistance and consider operation at full load and unity power factor.

The induced emf (line-to-line) is close to
questions.explanation:
Rated output power \(=S = 1000kVA\)
Rated line to line voltage \(=V_{l-l} = 6.6kV\)
Rated current,
\[\begin{aligned} I_a &=\frac{S}{\sqrt{3}V_{l-l}} \\ &= \frac{1000}{\sqrt{3} \times 6.6}\\ &=87.477A \end{aligned}\]
As generator is star connected.
Phase to neutral voltage
\[\begin{aligned} V_t &=\frac{V_{l-l}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ &= \frac{6.6}{\sqrt{3} }\\ &=3.81kV \end{aligned}\]
Taking \(V_t\) as the reference
\[\begin{aligned} V_t &=3.81 \angle 0^{\circ}kV\\ I_a&= 87.477\angle 0^{\circ}A\\ E_f &=V_t+I_a X_s \\ &= 3.81 \angle 0^{\circ}+ 87.477 \angle 0^{\circ} \\ &\times (j20) \times 10^{-3} \\ &= 4.19\angle 24.6^{\circ}kV \end{aligned}\]
Induced emf(line to line)
\[\begin{aligned} &=\sqrt{3}E_f \\ &= \sqrt{3} \times 4.19\\ &=7.2 kV \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
At a 220 kV substation of a power system, it is given that the three-phase fault level is 4000 MVA and single-line to ground fault level is 5000 MVA Neglecting the resistance and the shunt suspectances of the system.

The positive sequence driving point reactance at the bus is
questions.explanation:
Fault level (in MVA) = \(\sqrt{3} \times\) prefault line voltage (kV) \(\times\) fault current (in kA)
Pre-fault line voltage \(=V_{prefault}=220kV\)
\[\begin{aligned} 3-\phi \text{ fault level} &=4000 MVA \\ \sqrt{3} V_{present}I_f&=4000MVA \\ I_f&=\frac{4000 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3}\times 220 \times 10^3}\\ &=10.5kA \end{aligned}\]
Let positive sequence driving point reactance =\(=X_1\)
\[\begin{aligned} X_1&=\frac{V_{present}/\sqrt{3}}{I_f}\\ X_1&=\frac{220/\sqrt{3}}{10.5}=12.1\Omega \end{aligned}\]

questions.question:
At a 220 kV substation of a power system, it is given that the three-phase fault level is 4000 MVA and single-line to ground fault level is 5000 MVA Neglecting the resistance and the shunt suspectances of the system.

The zero sequence driving point reactance at the bus is
questions.explanation:
Let negative sequence reactance \(=X_2\)
Assuming, \(X_2=X_1\)
and zero sequence reactance \(=X_0\)
In single-line to ground fault,
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Fault level (MVA)}&=5000MVA\\ \text{Fault current}&=I_f=\frac{\text{Fault-level}}{\sqrt{3} \times V_{prefault}}\\ &=\frac{5000 \times 10^6}{\sqrt{3} \times 220 \times 10^3}\\ &=13.12kA\\ \text{In SLG fault}\\ \text{Positive}& \text{ sequence current}\\ I_{a1}&=\frac{I_f}{3}=\frac{13.12}{3}=4.37kA\\ I_{a1}&=\frac{V_{prefault}(\text(per phase))}{X_1+X_2+X_0}\\ 4.37&=\frac{220/\sqrt{3}}{2X_1+X_0}\\ &=\frac{127}{2 \times 12.1+X_0}\\ X_0&\approx 4.84\Omega \end{aligned}\]
